headline: A6's arm under-detected by an order of magnitude, and three successive defects were mine
source: peer_01 and peer_04, each applying A6 by hand against the bytes
what_happened: the arm as first written keyed on a field's own web: refs, so a gloss citing NO ref - which is exactly the class A6 exists to catch - was invisible. Widening it to the row's own span introduced a second defect: the reference to the row variable was STALE, because the row loop closes before the string loop, so every field would have been compared against the LAST row's span. Deriving the row from the field path index fixed it.

measured.peer_01_hand_audit: 34 qualifying runs across 13 of its 14 rows, longest 19 words, one a whole verse; the validator reported 0 for that group
measured.peer_04_hand_audit: 11 runs across 6 of its 13 rows, runs of 14/11/9/8/7/6 words; the validator reported 0 for that group

the_ruling_needed: the arm's 98 is still BELOW both peers' hand audits on their own rows, so the arm is a FLOOR and not a census. The author-wave worklist must therefore be built from the UNION of the arm's output and the peers' findings. Confirm that, or rule otherwise.
tier: MEASURED for every count; the extrapolation from two peers' rates to the corpus is INFERRED and is not offered as a figure

headline: A4 as implemented may be vacuous per-row, and a peer said so

A4's window [first-1, last+1] then reduces to exactly two verses - the onset seam and the close seam - and A4's own far-side clause bars per-row findings on the far side. peer_01's conclusion, in its words, is that A4 as implemented can never yield a per-row finding.
the_ruling_needed: is that the intended effect? A4 ordered the far-side fix corpus-wide, so a vacuous per-row arm may be exactly right - but if any per-row refs_mirror finding is meant to survive, the arm needs the onset seam explicitly exempted from the far-side bar.

headline: mark_symmetry is DIRECTION-BLIND, and the orchestrator's MARKS-3D patch did not fix that
source: peer_03, in its own words: the member tests whether a mark is disclosed, not which way it is read
what_happened: the MARKS-3D order was executed by labelling every flagged mark with its direction - onset seam, interior, close seam - and by making a span-scoped absence claim judge against the interior only. That removed a class of false positives and it is verifiable: flags fell from 12 to 8 and the two rows the ruling named as real are exactly the two that survive. But the arm still only asks whether a mark is MENTIONED near the row's reference. It never checks the row's CLAIM about direction. A row that discloses a mark and reads it backwards passes.
why_it_matters: peer_03 calls this the most consequential class it found, and its own two lanes split on an instance of it. The ruling's C1 wording makes direction-reading a PEER duty, so this round is covered - but nothing in the tooling will catch the class on a later book, and it costs a confidence level when it lands on a HIGH row.
the_ruling_needed: whether a directional-claim arm is a fifth tool order. The orchestrator's view, offered as a view and not a decision: the peer duty covers this book, and a tool arm is what makes it survive into Daniel, where the same mark layer is in force.
orchestrator_self_correction: an earlier report of mine said the MARKS-3D patch confirmed the controlling agent's analysis. That is true of the false-positive count and of the two real rows, and it is NOT true that the patch satisfies the whole order. peer_03 is right and the narrower claim is the accurate one.
tier: MEASURED for the flag counts; peer_03's characterisation REPORTED and accepted

headline: the A4 aggregate discrepancy is DIAGNOSED: the orchestrator's builder resolved adjacency on the WRONG NUMBERING FACE inside the zone
source: peer_05, which found the split wrong in both directions on one of its rows and named the cause
what_happened: the peer-scoping builder resolves a verse's neighbours from verse_inventory.json, which is WEB-numbered, while the zone prose argues on the MT face under oshb: prefixes. Ezekiel carries exactly one numbering zone - MT 21:1-5 = WEB 20:45-49 and MT 21:6-37 = WEB 21:1-32 - so inside chapters 20 and 21 an adjacency computed on the WEB face is simply the wrong verse. peer_05's P04-005 shows all three failure modes at once: the split calls one verse an in-window defect that the row mirrors explicitly, calls an already-mirrored in-span verse outside-window, and MISSES web:21:1 = MT 21:6 entirely - which is in window, argued as the second hard seam carrying the row's close, and absent from the reference list.
what_it_explains: this is the mechanism behind E13-05's three-way disagreement. The corrected tool and the builder both read the WEB face and land within 2 verses of each other (817 and 819); the ruling's 708 was reached by a different route. The zone is where a WEB-face computation must diverge, so a face error is the expected shape of this gap rather than a surprise.
what_it_does_NOT_settle: it does not establish which aggregate is right. It establishes that the orchestrator's two figures share a defect and should not be treated as two independent confirmations of each other.
action_taken: NONE to the scoping file: the running peers have it pinned by digest and mutating it would break their bindings. The correction belongs to the author-wave worklist, where the aggregate actually decides how many rows get a reference installed.
the_ruling_needed: the authoritative aggregate, computed zone-aware on the MT face where the prose argues there
tier: REPORTED by peer_05 with its verses named; the mechanism is MEASURED by it against the offset map

headline: THE ORCHESTRATOR'S LAUNCH HINTS CARRY AN ANCHORING RISK, and peer_06 demonstrated both the risk and the correct response
source: peer_06, in its own words: contrary to the pattern I was warned to expect
what_happened: as each peer landed, the orchestrator folded its findings into the next peer's launch message. The hints surfaced real checks - several peers found classes they say they would not have run otherwise - but they also tell a lane what to expect BEFORE it measures. peer_06 was warned the A6 class was pervasive, measured its own rows, found ZERO qualifying runs across eight of its fourteen (all three of its hits are in one cluster), and said so explicitly against the expectation it had been given.
the_risk_named_honestly: a hint is an input to a lane, and a hint that describes a RESULT rather than a CHECK invites the lane to confirm it. A weaker lane than peer_06 might have found the pattern because it was told the pattern existed. The orchestrator introduced this and it is not something a peer asked for.
mitigation_applied: from peer_10 onward the launch message states the checks and explicitly says they are checks worth running rather than results to expect, names peer_06's contradiction as the model response, and says that if a lane's rows do not show a pattern the honest answer is that they do not
the_ruling_needed: whether accumulating cross-peer hints is permitted at all in a round whose value comes from independence, or whether later peers should be launched blind to earlier findings and the accumulated checks instead routed into the author wave. The orchestrator has a view - the checks are worth more than the anchoring costs, given peer_06 resisted - but this is a design question about the round and belongs to the controlling agent.
tier: MEASURED by peer_06 for its own rows; the anchoring RISK is INFERRED and is the orchestrator's own assessment of its own conduct

Here the ANSWER was right and both GROUNDS were wrong, so any process that validated conclusions by agreement would have recorded a sound finding resting on two false warrants. Only a lens that went to the bytes could tell.

headline: refs_mirror cannot see an IN-SPAN argued-but-unmirrored verse AT ALL, and a peer found nine
what_happened: the checker computes missing = argued - covered - own_span, so it SUBTRACTS the row's own span before flagging. A verse that the prose argues, that the reference list omits, and that lies INSIDE the span is therefore invisible to the member by construction. peer_06 found nine such verses by hand. peer_06 also traced the root cause of one flagged mark gap to exactly this: the row's own CLOSE verse is missing from its own boundary_evidence_refs, so the mark had nothing to attach to.
reading: this completes the detection picture. E13-03 reported the member missing in-window verses; this says the in-SPAN class is structurally outside its reach, which is a larger hole and includes the row's own seam verses. Three peers separately report the member yields no per-row finding - and the reason may be that everything it could legitimately find has been subtracted away.
the_ruling_needed: whether own_span should stop being subtracted, which is a one-line change with a corpus-wide blast radius and must not be made without the controlling agent's ruling
tier: MEASURED by peer_06 by hand; the mechanism is MEASURED by the orchestrator in the tool's source

headline: CROSS-PEER CONTAMINATION: concurrent peers wrote helper scripts into a shared scratchpad namespace and two were OVERWRITTEN MID-EXECUTION
source: peer_07, which detected it and re-verified its own figures
what_happened: peer_07 reports that two helper scripts it had written into the session scratchpad were replaced mid-run by a different peer's files of the same names, identifiable by the other peer's row list. peer_07 re-ran its A6 audit from a self-contained script importing no helper; it reproduced exactly - 1273 verses, identical per-row distribution - and its deliverable builder imports no helper, so none of its figures depend on a changed file.
why_it_is_high: the two colliding parsers differ PRECISELY in multi-line translation-verse handling, which is the failure mode that already caused one peer to understate its own audit. peer_07 protected itself and states plainly that it cannot check any other peer and is forbidden to read their output. So for every other peer that used a helper script, whether its figures were computed by its own parser or by another peer's is UNKNOWN to me.
root_cause_is_mine: the PRIMARIES' brief required each agent to write private working files into a uniquely named subdirectory of its own scratchpad, and every primary reported doing so. I did not carry that instruction into the peer brief. The collision is my omission, not a peer's error.
action_taken: the three peers still running were sent the hazard, told to isolate private files under a uniquely named subdirectory, told to re-verify any helper-dependent figure from a self-contained script, told the multi-line failure mode and the correct 1273 total, and told to report a figure they cannot vouch for as UNAVAILABLE rather than as measured. peer_11's launch carries the instruction. PEER_BRIEF_EZEK.md was NOT edited: the running peers verify its digest, and changing it mid-round would break their pins.
the_ruling_needed: whether the landed peers' helper-dependent figures need re-verification, and whether any peer must be re-run. The orchestrator cannot determine which landed peers used helpers without reading transcripts it is told not to read, so this is a scope decision.
carry_forward: per-agent private subdirectories belong in the standing method, not in one book's brief. This is a lane-isolation defect: concurrent agents in one shared writable namespace.
tier: REPORTED by peer_07 with its own re-verification MEASURED; the exposure of other peers is UNKNOWN

headline: the dateline month-ordinal field is WITHDRAWN to UNAVAILABLE after two opposite failures
source: peer_07 found the first; checking its report exposed the second
what_happened: v1 matched a DAY numeral as a month ordinal wherever the day word's stem collided with a compound ordinal's first word - wrong at MT 26:1, which peer_07 reported independently. v2 stripped the day numeral, fixed MT 26:1, and BROKE MT 24:1 and MT 32:1, both of which genuinely name a month, because the phrase extractor truncates at the FIRST month word and so cuts the phrase before the ordinal it is hunting.
resolution: v3 keeps the two fields that were MEASURED and never in doubt - the year term and the month word - publishes the FULL date phrase to the LAST month word so nothing is truncated, and writes the month ordinal as UNAVAILABLE with the reason. A third positional rule would be a guess presented as a measurement. v1 and v2 are kept on disk.
lesson_against_myself: routing a field for ratification while ALSO publishing my own answer for it invited the reliance the routing existed to prevent. If another party is to determine a value, publish the evidence and leave the value empty. Also: v1 asserted the ruling's single ground-truth vector and reproduced it, then published - one vector tested one path and passed while the detector was broken for another verse.
tier: the two surviving fields MEASURED; the withdrawn field UNAVAILABLE by the orchestrator's own admission

headline: a sixth group confirms web_quotes misses the gloss-shaped run specifically
measured: web_quotes reported ZERO for all 11 of its rows; peer_07 measures 5 substantive qualifying runs on 4 rows, three missing BOTH the curly quotes and the in-field reference. It also measures 7 other runs, up to 44 words, that ARE correctly handled.
reading: the 44-word compliant runs are the important part: the authors knew the convention and applied it to long quotations. What the member misses is the GLOSS-SHAPED run - short, unquoted, woven into prose - which is precisely the class A6 was written for. peer_07 also parsed the translation with multi-line verse bodies joined BEFORE auditing, and reports 1273 verses equal to the Hebrew.

headline: a third group measures the in-window class the member omits, and names the mechanism

headline: the universals arm's context window does not always contain the claim it flags
measured: 15 genuine of 43, collapsing to 9 distinct objects - a fifth distinct rate. And on 5 of the 43 the flag's own context window does not contain the claim being flagged; on the one genuine instance in that set, a reviewer reading the context alone would CLEAR it.
why_it_matters: this is a different defect from the false-positive rate. A flag whose context does not contain its own claim cannot be answered from the flag - the answerer must go find the claim - and a reviewer who trusts the context will answer it wrongly in the safe-looking direction. It makes the member's output unreliable as a worklist even where the flag is genuine.

headline: A DESIGN CONSEQUENCE THREE LANES HIT INDEPENDENTLY: one field can carry work from two different sweeps, so a few edits pool an A6 component into an A4-labelled edit and the per-sweep parity digits attribute them to one sweep
status: OPEN - recorded; affects parity reporting, not correctness
the_mechanism: authors work by ROW because judgement needs the whole row, and the orchestrator applies by SWEEP because #e13 orders the sweeps and E-18 wants parity digits per sweep. When a citation install and a quotation repair land on the SAME field of the same row, they cannot be two independent edits: a later whole-field set cannot survive an earlier append, and an append cannot carry the repair. So the lane emits ONE edit doing both.

measured.lane_02: 1 edit (P01-013), labelled a4, carrying one a6 component
measured.lane_05: 3 edits pooling an a6 item into an a4 or grounds edit
measured.lane_06: 2 edits (P10-012, P10-013), set-on-refs rather than appends

why_it_is_not_a_correctness_problem: the final text is the same either way, every such edit names its expected_before exactly, and all three lanes' plans validate in sweep order under simulation. What is affected is the ATTRIBUTION in the per-sweep parity digits: six edits do work belonging to two sweeps and are counted under one.
what_i_will_do: report the pooling explicitly in each sweep's receipt, naming the edits that carry a second sweep's component, so the parity digits are not read as a clean per-class count when they are not. All three lanes offered to separate them if I would rather re-pool; I will not, because splitting them would require an edit whose expected_before cannot be stated until the other has been applied - which is strictly more fragile.
for_daniel: the sweep unit should be (sweep, field) rather than sweep, or the deliverable schema should let one edit declare several sweep components. Three independent lanes hitting this in one wave makes it a design flaw and not an accident.

headline: THE A4 CLASS IS INCOMPLETE BY ~53 CITATIONS ON 22 ROWS: my member cannot see a DOTTED CONTINUATION of a citation list, and neither can the controlling agent's recount - so the 292-for-292 set equality confirmed my code and not my reading of the definition

the_gap: the member's patterns are an Ezek.C.V token, a bare C:V cite with a COLON, an 'MT C:V' qualifier, and a v./vv. expression. A DOTTED continuation of an OSIS-style list - '20.14' in 'oshb:Ezek.20.9, 20.14 and 20.22' - matches none of them, so the member takes the first member of such a list and drops the rest.
THE_LESSON_AND_IT_IS_THE_BIGGEST_OF_THIS: my P2 distinct check matched the controlling agent's independent recount at SET EQUALITY, 292 items for 292, row by row and verse list by verse list, zero differences. I reported that as strong evidence, and it was - for the wrong proposition. Both implementations read DEF-A4-ARGUED clause 1's enumeration of citation FORMS, and that enumeration omits the dotted continuation. Two independently written implementations of ONE DEFINITION are ONE LENS: they agree exactly because they share the definition's blind spot, and their agreement measures code fidelity rather than coverage of the corpus. The decorrelated lens that found this was an author reading the PROSE OF A ROW instead of the specification. OW-19 says a third lens counts only if DECORRELATED; this is that principle one level deeper than I had applied it, and I had explicitly called the recount decorrelated.
why_the_reading_that_fixes_it_is_not_a_d: clause 1 opens 'Any verse anchor a prose field carries' and then names four forms. The governing phrase is the first one; the four forms illustrate it. A dotted continuation of a list IS a verse anchor a prose field carries, and clause 2 already makes a comma/'and' list one citation PER MEMBER - so a three-verse list is three citations whatever the members' spelling. I am therefore implementing clause 1's rule rather than extending it, AND routing the reading for confirmation, because an incomplete Tier-0 gate is red at the close either way and the safer error is to over-disclose the interpretation.

extend the member to read a dotted continuation in an OSIS list context; add fixtures for the three-member list and for the decimal that must NOT match
re-run over the POST-WAVE rows and distinct-check the delta

headline: A CONTROL THAT WORKED AND SHOULD BE KEPT: the harness's per-sweep preimage backup is what let me measure the baseline after the fact
what_happened: I ran the validator suite for the first time AFTER mutating 137 rows, so I had no baseline and could not distinguish a flag the wave caused from one it inherited. The guarded mutation harness writes a preimage backup before every sweep it applies; ten of them were on disk, including the original at 25cdba56. I recovered the pre-wave corpus from that backup and ran the suite on it.
why_it_matters: the backup existed because the harness keeps one per sweep as a matter of course, not because I anticipated needing it. Without it the honest report would have been 'three checks are red and I cannot tell you whether the wave did it'.
the_lesson: a cheap, unconditional, per-step artifact beats a planned one, because the thing you need it for is by definition the thing you did not plan for. And: RUN THE GATE BEFORE THE MUTATION. Measuring the baseline is one command and I skipped it.

headline: FOR THE CONTROLLING AGENT: the citation sweep's Hebrew arm locates each run with find(), so two byte-identical runs in one field are BOTH judged at the first one's position. That is the blind spot that let the orchestrator's wrong-verse repair pass every byte check.
the_mechanism: the arm finds a Hebrew run's position with a first-match search, then collates it against the references near THAT position. Where the same run appears twice in one field, the second occurrence is judged in the first's neighbourhood.
what_it_hid: my Hebrew repair gave both occurrences of one word Ezek.5.7's bytes although the second occurrence's clause attributes it to Ezek.5.10. It passed every byte check and every collation check, because the second run was judged where the first one stood.
it_still_bites: after the remediation agent's fix the row is byte-correct for both verses, but MT 5:8 and MT 5:10 carry identical therefore-head bytes, so the 5:10 run is still checked in 5:8's neighbourhood. It passes and it is correct - and NO GATE PROTECTS THAT CLASS.
the_proposed_fix: finditer with per-match offsets, so each occurrence is collated at its own position
why_it_matters_beyond_this_row: a checker that judges the second instance at the first's position cannot see a wrong-verse attribution in any field carrying a repeated formula - and this book's prose repeats formulae constantly, because that is what its boundaries are made of

headline: FOR THE CONTROLLING AGENT: a TRUE ABSENCE CLAIM about a paseq is UNWRITABLE in the ROLE vocabulary - the sweep's paseq arm has no negation guard and the DISCLOSURE-paseq token itself supplies the device name that fires it
the_mechanism: the paseq arm fires whenever the device name appears anywhere in an annotation and the census is empty at that verse. It has no adjacent-negation guard - unlike the puncta arm, which does. And [DISCLOSURE-paseq] itself contains the device name, so the token alone trips it.
consequence: 'no paseq stands here' cannot be written with the token whose job is paseq disclosure
what_the_agent_did: used [ANCHOR]: 'oshb:Ezek.41.9 [ANCHOR] device census records no stroke here (single-witness, tier-3)'. Not WARRANT-absence-over-range, because the claim is single-verse rather than over a range, and the row's own prose says stroke density is never a boundary argument - so a WARRANT token would be a defect under the role rule.
the_question_for_the_ruling: if absence claims are to be expressible at all, the paseq arm needs the adjacent-negation guard the puncta arm already has, or the vocabulary needs a single-verse absence token. The agent's ANCHOR reading is defensible and is not a substitute for that decision.
